avoma-alternatives.0: Avoma bundles a lot into one product: an AI meeting assistant, a scheduler, conversation intelligence and revenue intelligence. That bundle is its strength. It is also the reason sales teams start searching for Avoma alternatives, because once you add the Conversation Intelligence and Revenue Intelligence add-ons, the per-seat cost climbs fast.
avoma-alternatives.1: Below: 6 Avoma alternatives for US sales teams, with prices, strengths and the trade-off you take with each one.
avoma-alternatives.2: On yearly billing, Avoma costs $19 per recorder seat per month on Startup and $29 on Organization, or $29 and $39 billed monthly. Enterprise is $39 billed yearly with a 10-seat minimum. View-only seats? Free ([Avoma pricing](https://www.avoma.com/pricing)).
avoma-alternatives.3: A rep on Organization with both intelligence add-ons costs $87 a month billed yearly, which for a 10-rep team comes to $10,440 a year. That number usually triggers the search for Avoma competitors.
avoma-alternatives.4: Cost at scale is the top reason, since coaching and forecasting features sit in add-ons that roughly triple the base seat price. Other common reasons:
avoma-alternatives.5: Avoma is an AI meeting assistant built for revenue teams. In one platform it combines 4 products: an AI note taker, a scheduler with lead routing, conversation intelligence for coaching, and revenue intelligence for deals and forecasting. Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams calls are all recorded, and notes sync to CRMs.
avoma-alternatives.6: The bundle works well when a team uses most of it. Using only the note taker? Then it gets expensive.
avoma-alternatives.7: When your team uses at least 2 of its 4 modules and stays under its seat caps (25 paid seats on Startup, 100 on Organization), Avoma is enough. Mid-sized sales teams that want one vendor for notes, scheduling and coaching fit it well.
avoma-alternatives.9: Before you switch, run a 2-week pilot with 3 to 5 reps and real calls. Keep it short and structured. That avoids a painful migration later.
avoma-alternatives.11: Recording happens through a bot on Zoom, Google Meet and Teams, or without a bot through the Mac app and Chrome extension, including in-person meetings. Scheduling? Calendly and Cal.com. Free covers 5 notes a month; Pro is $15 a month.
avoma-alternatives.13: Gong is the category leader for revenue intelligence: deal boards, forecasting and coaching at scale. Pricing is quote-based and typically aimed at larger sales organizations, so choose Gong if you use Avoma's Revenue Intelligence add-on heavily and have budget.
avoma-alternatives.14: Fireflies records calls, syncs notes into CRMs and searches across every conversation. Pro costs $10 per seat billed yearly and Business $19 ([Fireflies help center](https://guide.fireflies.ai/articles/3734844560-learn-about-the-fireflies-pricing-plans)). Most of what reps use Avoma's base plan for is covered, at a lower price.
avoma-alternatives.17: Read AI scores engagement and talk time and offers a meeting coach, while Pro costs $15 billed yearly and includes Salesforce and HubSpot integrations. More in [Read AI pricing](https://lynkk.ai/blog/read-ai-pricing).
avoma-alternatives.19: Yearly billing for Lynkk saves 35% during early-bird pricing, lowering its real cost further. Whichever you pick, price the add-ons you actually need. Not the headline seat.
avoma-alternatives.20: Every Avoma alternative trades something away. Here is what you gain, and what you give up, with each one.
avoma-alternatives.25: Avoma vs Otter is a sales platform versus a transcription tool. Scheduling, conversation intelligence and revenue intelligence are what Avoma adds, whereas Otter focuses on live transcripts and summaries, with sales features on its higher plans.
avoma-alternatives.27: Avoma vs Copilot comes down to scope. Microsoft 365 Copilot summarizes Teams meetings and works across Microsoft apps, but it is not a sales tool: no deal boards, scorecards or scheduler. By contrast, Avoma is built for revenue teams and works across Zoom, Meet and Teams.
avoma-alternatives.30: Avoma is worth it for sales teams of roughly 10 to 100 reps that use its note taker, scheduler and at least 1 intelligence add-on, because one vendor replaces 2 or 3 tools. For teams that only need meeting notes, or for very large revenue organizations that need enterprise forecasting, it rarely is.
avoma-alternatives.31: Run the numbers on your own usage. A rep on Organization with Conversation Intelligence costs $58 a month billed yearly, and if the coaching features change how managers coach, that is cheap. Nobody opens the scorecards? Then the same $58 buys a note taker plus a separate scheduler with money left over.
avoma-alternatives.37: Fireflies and Fathom Business are the best lower-cost Avoma alternatives with CRM sync. Gong is the best for enterprise revenue intelligence, and Lynkk is the best for call prep, live answers and follow-up tasks. Mainly use Avoma as a note taker? A cheaper tool usually covers it. Rely on its forecasting? Compare Gong instead.
